A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SVIP despite the revised title and experimental focus. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and matching algorithms and retained results support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 3 and the appendices report original timing, acceptance-rate and entropy analyses, including SpecBench, long-form generation, GliDe/CaPE and EAGLE-2 experiments.

after.justification: Sections 2–3 report original rejection analyses, MT-Bench experiments and QwQ reasoning results on MATH, AIME and GPQA. Appendix D also retains original greedy-decoding results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same entropy-threshold stopping rule, and Appendix A retains the verification and correction procedures. The newly distilled QwQ draft model supplies an experimental configuration; it does not establish a change to SVIP's procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds long-form mathematical and scientific reasoning evaluation on MATH, AIME 2022–2024 and GPQA, plus mathematical Persona data for draft-model distillation. MT-Bench remains, but the dedicated SpecBench and earlier multi-domain integration evaluations, including translation, summarization, finance and SQL tasks, are removed.

E2.justification: The GliDe and GliDe+CaPE comparisons in v1 Table 3 are removed entirely. Constant-length, Hugging Face heuristic and EAGLE-2 comparisons remain, while v2 Figure 7(a) adds fixed-length 2–4 controls alongside length 5. AdaEAGLE is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: MT-Bench evaluation replaces the Pythia/Qwen/LLaMA configuration set with six Qwen2.5 target–draft combinations. V2 tunes h=0.3 once and reuses it, replacing model-specific threshold selection. EAGLE-2 evaluation now varies context length on Vicuna, and the new reasoning protocol specifies 200 MATH questions, 73 AIME questions and GPQA Diamond.

E4.justification: V2 adds rejection-position KL and vocabulary diagnostics, oracle-length variability and mismatch analyses, shorter fixed-length controls, and token-level and generation case studies. It removes v1's SpecBench acceptance-length analyses and entropy-ratio/scatter plots across three model families. The Qwen greedy-decoding comparison in Appendix D is retained.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports averaging three repetitions for Pythia and Qwen, with different seeds where applicable; v2 omits this information without establishing that fewer runs occurred. V2 Figure 1 newly displays oracle-length standard deviations, describing length variability rather than uncertainty in speedup estimates. Neither version reports speedup confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Many benchmark results are removed or replaced, and QwQ reasoning results are added. For Qwen2.5 14B/0.5B at 8K, v1 Table 2 reports SVIP/constant speedups of 1.35/1.04, versus 1.36/1.23 in v2 Figure 5; missing execution details preclude treating this as a controlled performance change. The 24 Qwen greedy-decoding values from v1 Table 6 remain identical in v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: The Pinsker and Bretagnolle–Huber bounds remain, but v2 substantially extends the approximation analysis. Section 2.2 and new Appendix C introduce the random entropy ratio, the sufficient conservativeness condition gamma <= 2c + 1, and validity-probability derivations under Gaussian and shifted-Gamma assumptions. This qualifies and extends v1's empirical constant approximation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift from broad SpecBench and cross-framework acceleration to long-form generation, reasoning and test-time scaling. Headline claims change from approximately 20% SpecBench and 60% long-form gains to 17% MT-Bench and 22% QwQ gains, and rejection analysis becomes an explicit contribution. The training-free entropy-policy claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 introduces substantive interpretations involving abrupt rejection, excess drafting relative to oracle lengths, and the difficulty of reasoning keywords compared with subword completions. Its new Limitations section discusses conservative bounds and unmodeled context-dependent patterns and model biases. The warning about repetitive greedy generation inflating speedups was already present in v1.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's code link, GPU specifications and EAGLE-2 detail about checking entropy every two draft tokens; the omission does not establish an implementation change. It adds the QwQ draft model's initialization and one-million-example distillation source, but provides only a promise of a future model link, without training hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The three-category related-work organization remains. V2 adds AdaEAGLE and explicit training-free contrasts, references supporting the reasoning experiments and temperature discussion, and a claim to first investigate EAGLE-2 in long-form generation. References associated with the removed Pythia, LLaMA and attention-throughput discussion disappear.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the title, abstract, introduction and method narrative, leading with rejection investigation instead of speculative-decoding preliminaries. Experiments are reorganized around long-form generation and reasoning, Appendix C changes from additional SpecBench results to approximation theory, and a Limitations section is added.

P2.justification: The motivating illustration is replaced by a redesigned method overview and an oracle-length plot. New rejection, speedup, oracle-gap and case-study plots substantially change the visual presentation. Reasoning and token-statistics tables are added, EAGLE-2 results are reorganized by context length, and most earlier SpecBench tables and bar charts disappear.

improvement.justification: The shorter-length controls, rejection analyses and conditional approximation derivation strengthen the paper's explanatory support. However, removing hardware, repetition and access information weakens reproducibility of the revised timing evidence. V2 also claims a 22% AIME improvement in the introduction, whereas Table 3 implies about 12% from 1.77 versus 1.58; approximately 22% applies to GPQA. These material gains and reporting regressions leave the net quality change uncertain.
